inline_comments.comment: `std-env` is imported here but is not declared in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`'s `dependencies`. Per project rules, each workspace `package.json` must explicitly declare every package it imports directly. Relying on it being available transitively through the workspace root or another package is fragile and can break depending on the package manager's hoisting behavior. Add `"std-env": "<version>"` to `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`.

This `logger.log` call runs unconditionally for every user who runs `npx create storybook`, not only in agent environments. Every non-agent user will see output like "Detecting agent presence: unknown" during a normal install. This is a debugging artifact and must be removed before merging. The conditional `if (isAgent)` block on the lines that follow already logs a relevant message when an agent is actually detected, so this unconditional line provides no additional value.

When `skipPrompt` is `true` (triggered by `--yes` or any non-interactive flag), this returns `true`, causing `Feature.AI` to be included and `@storybook/addon-mcp` to be installed without the user ever being asked. Someone using `--yes` for CI, scripted installs, or to simply skip prompts would unexpectedly get an extra addon. The safe default for opt-in features in non-interactive mode is `false`. If agent-driven flows should always include the AI feature, that logic belongs in `initiate.ts` where `options.agent` is already checked, not here where `skipPrompt` is a broader signal.

This dynamic import crosses the `create-storybook` → `cli-storybook` package boundary via a deep relative path into the other package's `src/` directory. Per project conventions, cross-package calls must go through the consuming package's declared public export (e.g., the `@storybook/cli` package name or an explicit subpath entry point), not through relative source paths. Deep relative cross-package imports bypass the target package's API surface and silently break under any file restructuring. Add a proper exports entry in `cli-storybook/package.json` and import via that path instead.

Project convention requires using `logger` from `storybook/internal/node-logger` instead of `console.*` in server-side code under `code/lib/**`. The markdown output (line 55) should use `logger.log(generateMarkdownOutput(projectInfo))`. For the JSON output, if a clean stdout stream without any logger prefix is required so consumers can pipe or parse it directly, that intent should be documented with an inline comment — and `process.stdout.write` is more semantically explicit for raw machine-readable output than `console.log`.

`framework`, `renderer`, and `builder` are typed as `string | null`, but in `ai/index.ts` each is assigned via `data.frameworkPackage ?? 'unknown'` (and equivalents), meaning they are always a non-null string in practice. The `null` branch is never populated, making it misleading for downstream consumers who might add unnecessary null-guards. Change these to `string` (using `'unknown'` as the sentinel for a missing value), which also aligns with how the prompt templates in `prompt.ts` already use these fields without null checks.

The JSDoc comment reads "Represents a skill category that can be expanded in the future. Each skill provides..." but the interface is named `AiPrompt`, not `Skill`. This is a leftover from when this type was named `Skill`. Update the comment to accurately describe `AiPrompt`, for example: "A named AI prompt with a description and step-by-step instructions for agent-driven Storybook setup."

The generated code example labels the file as `preview.ts` but the decorator body contains JSX (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<MemoryRouter>`, `<Story />`). A `.ts` file does not support JSX syntax by default — TypeScript will emit a parse error unless the file is renamed to `preview.tsx` or `"jsx": "react-jsx"` (or equivalent) is set in `tsconfig.json`. The example filename in the comment and code fence should be `preview.tsx`, or a note should be added explaining the TSConfig requirement. This issue exists in both the CSF Factory and standard CSF branches of `getPreviewConfigExample`.

general_comments.comment: None of the new AI modules (`ai/index.ts`, `ai/prompt.ts`) have any automated tests, and the PR checklist marks all testing categories unchecked. Several pure functions in `prompt.ts` — `getDocsUrl`, `generateMarkdownOutput`, `generateJsonOutput`, `getPrompts` — are straightforward to unit test with input/output assertions. Key behaviors that should be covered include: `getDocsUrl` with `undefined`, `9`, and `10` as inputs; the early-return path for non-React-Vite frameworks; CSF Factory vs. standard CSF branch selection in the generated output. Additionally, `UserPreferencesCommand.test.ts` should be updated with a case for `Feature.AI`, and `AddonService.test.ts` should verify that `Feature.AI` maps to `@storybook/addon-mcp`.

In `code/lib/create-storybook/src/generators/types.ts`, the comment on the new `agent` property reads `// Whether this is being run via an ai agent`. 'ai' should be 'AI' to match the casing used everywhere else in this PR — the enum value `Feature.AI`, the telemetry event `'ai-init'`, and the CLI subcommand `storybook ai`.
